subject: Biology
title: Unicellular and Multicellular Organisms
summary: An amoeba is one cell; you are about 37 trillion. In one, a single cell does everything; in the other, cells share the work.
keyPoints: **Unicellular:** the whole body is one cell, which carries out every life process (Amoeba, Paramecium, bacteria).
**Division of labour:** specialised cells do different jobs (muscle, nerve, red blood cells).
Every multicellular organism starts as **one cell, the zygote**.

blocks.alt: An amoeba as one cell beside a block of many cells
blocks.caption: One cell does everything, or many cells share the work.

blocks.p: In an **Amoeba** the single cell takes in food, respires, removes waste and reproduces by dividing. Your body has about **37 trillion** cells (an estimate).

blocks.alt: Muscle cells, a nerve cell and red blood cells
blocks.caption: Each cell's shape suits its job.

blocks.p: A multicellular organism develops from a single cell, the **zygote**, which divides again and again (1 → 2 → 4 → 8 …); the cells then specialise.

quiz.explain: Paramecium's whole body is one cell.

options: Different cells are specialised for different jobs
quiz.explain: In multicellular organisms, specialised cells share the body's work.

quiz.q: Which cell carries oxygen in the blood?
A zygote divides into two every hour. Starting from one cell, how many after 5 hours?

quiz.explain: It develops from one cell, the zygote.
